title: Leg vein ultrasound
also: venous duplex scan of the legs
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at the veins in your legs: how blood flows, whether the valves work, and whether there are any blood clots. It is safe and uses no radiation.
why: For swelling, heavy legs, spider veins and varicose veins, before vein surgery, or if a blood clot is suspected.
tell_doctor: If you have had blood clots or vein surgery
If one leg has suddenly swollen and hurts right now. This needs to be checked urgently

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: No special preparation is needed. You can eat and drink as usual.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear comfortable clothes that are easy to take off down to your underwear. On this day, take off compression stockings before the scan.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not put cream on your legs on the day of the scan.

bring: Past vein ultrasound reports, if you have them
A towel to wipe off the gel
steps: You take off your clothes from your legs, down to your underwear
Part of the scan is done standing. This way the veins fill with blood better
The doctor puts on gel and moves the probe from your groin down to your foot
Sometimes the doctor squeezes your leg by hand or asks you to strain
Then the scan continues while you lie down
feel: The probe presses a little. It usually does not hurt
You will need to stand for a few minutes. If you feel dizzy, say so
after: The gel is wiped off, and you can go about your day right away
You usually get the report right away
Talk about further treatment with your doctor
red_flags: Sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, or coughing up blood: call emergency services
One leg suddenly swells, hurts, and turns red

faq.q: Can a vein ultrasound show a blood clot?
faq.a: Yes. Ultrasound is the main way to find a blood clot in the leg veins.

faq.q: Why is a vein ultrasound done standing?
faq.a: When you stand, the veins fill with blood, and the doctor can see where the valves let blood flow backward.
